topic: recursive properly weighted priority resampling for multi-generation rare-event trees

public_evidence.source: Finke, Johansen, Lee, Murray, Resampling in conditional SMC algorithms
public_evidence.result: The paper defines a resampling law rho over dependent ancestor indices, an explicit index distribution lambda, and post-resampling factor phi(m,n,u)=W^n lambda(m,u|n)/(M^{-1}rho^m(n,u)). Proper weighting plus persistence suffices for valid SMC normalizing-constant estimates and covers adaptive/systematic resampling without exchangeability.

derived_results.claim: Let r_n=sum_m P(A^m=n)=E[N_n|current particle system] be the expected offspring count of parent n under any dependent resampling law. Use the balanced index distribution lambda(m,du|n)=rho^m(n,du)/r_n. Substitution into Finke's phi gives post-resampling weight tilde w^m=W^n/r_n whenever A^m=n. If the priority resampler is designed so r_n=M q_n, this becomes exactly W^n/(M q_n), independent of which descendant slot selected n and independent of ancestor-index dependence.

A recursive multi-generation construction is therefore available: at each generation compute a predictable defensive priority q with q_n>=eW_n; generate M dependent ancestors with a stratified resampling law whose expected counts are Mq; assign each selected child W_n/(Mq_n); propagate under the base transition kernel and multiply the ordinary next-step potential/likelihood; normalize and repeat. The floor makes r_n>0 whenever W_n>0, satisfying the support side of proper weighting, while positive M/persistence prevents all postweights vanishing. Under the paper's SMC framework this preserves unbiased normalizing-constant estimation despite dependent sibling selection.

The resampling law and its ingredients may depend on the current weighted particle system. Thus semantic/proxy priority scores computed from current trajectory prefixes can define q before the current resampling randomness without breaking the proper-weighting formula. Future-outcome adaptation still belongs to the next generation, not the current draw.

The W/(Mq) factor corrects only ancestor/branch selection. If a child environment/tool response is generated from proposal transition Q rather than base transition P, the child must additionally carry the usual P/Q transition likelihood ratio wherever identifiable. Recursive resampling validity does not repair a missing environment likelihood ratio.

Both systematic and stratified q-resampling can fit the proper-weighting architecture when their exact rho/lambda are used; correctness does not pick the more efficient scheme. r120 plus the Douc counterexample favors independent stratification as a robust default because it weakly lowers one-step variance while systematic can alias with ordering.

portable_algorithm: Compute positive priority score a_n and q0_n proportional to W_n a_n.
Choose M before current resampling; stratify the CDF of q with independent uniforms, producing dependent ancestor vector A and expected counts Mq.
For child m with ancestor n, set pre-transition unnormalized weight W_n/(M q_n).
Propagate child under base dynamics P; multiply next potential/likelihood. If using a proposed transition Q, also multiply P/Q.
Normalize child weights and repeat. Keep actual q, M and transition proposal metadata in provenance so the weight can be audited.
negative_or_scope_evidence: The simplification W/(Mq) assumes the balanced index distribution and expected offspring counts r_n=Mq_n. An arbitrary dependent resampler with a different indexed law must use its actual Finke phi rather than this shortcut.

A current-generation output-dependent particle count is not proven safe by this fixed-M balanced derivation; choose M before current resampling or use a dedicated random-count proper-weighting construction.
Unbiased normalizing-constant estimation is a correctness property, not a guarantee that semantic priority lowers variance in every environment.
Transition-law proposal bias remains a separate identifiability requirement.
next_tests: Implement a 2-5 generation synthetic tree comparing iid and stratified priority resampling under identical q and base transitions; verify normalizing-constant mean and quantify cumulative variance reduction.
Construct the systematic comb/order counterexample in the priority notation and test whether random permutation restores performance at extra compute cost.
Connect predictable M to r119 evidence demand: derive a value-of-information rule for buying extra descendants while M is chosen before current outcomes.
Study weight/ESS collapse across generations under aggressive scores and determine whether the defensive floor should adapt predictably from past ESS plus certification state.
Only after transition P/Q is available or the environment stays at base, map the construction to multi-turn agent trajectory evaluation.
